title.narrative: Green Transition Portfolio med UNDP - Phase 1
Green Transition Portfolio w UNDP - Phase 1

description.narrative: Green Transition Portfolio syftar till att bidra till en rättvis grön omställning i Bosnien och Hercegovina genom att ge beslutsfattare, företag, samhällen, entreprenörer och forskare möjlighet att utforma och implementera policyer och lösningar som driver betydande koldioxidutsläpp och CO2-minskning.

The Green Transition Portfolio aims to contribute to a just green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina by empowering policymakers, businesses, communities, entrepreneurs, and scientists to devise and implement policies and solutions driving significant decarbonization and CO2 reduction.

The Portfolio aims to contribute to a just green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina by empowering policymakers, businesses, communities, entrepreneurs, and scientists to devise and implement policies and solutions driving significant decarbonization and CO2 reduction. Key focus areas include transitioning from fossil fuels to clean energy (aiming for the most vulnerable to escape energy poverty), eliminating waste and pollution, combating environmental harms, introducing circular and climate neutral business models, and protecting natural resources. The portfolio supports effective, fair, and sustainable development through policy dialogue, regulatory improvements, capacity building, and incentives in energy sustainability, waste management, sustainable business models, green chemistry, and environmental protection, driving system level changes for Bosnia and Herzegovinas green transition.
The strategic intent of the portfolio is to contribute to accelerated decarbonization and reduction of the CO2 footprint and green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with the following change hypothesis: By empowering and inspiring people policymakers, communities, businesses and entrepreneurs, scientists, innovators and coming together to implement new integrated solutions and policies that enable switching from fossil fuels to clean energy production and consumption, reduce waste and pollution, minimize environmental crimes, introduce circular business models, protect and replenish natural resources or nurture sustainable lifestyles in society.
The main underlying shifts that the socioeconomic systems in Bosnia and Herzegovina need to operate for a green transition are: A shift from a sectoral approach to policy design, financing and delivery towards outcome driven governance, which collaborates across mandates and with system stakeholders and applies a wholistic, just, gender sensitive and sustainable logic in legislative, policy and financing frameworks that catalyse the green and just transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina. A shift from extractive and linear economic models and fossil fuel dependency of the economy towards reduced pollution and greenhouse gas emissions, as well as circular and climate neutral business models that protect natural resources and biodiversity while ensuring economic growth decoupled from natural resources. A shift from communities with limited awareness and responsibility towards the environment and prevailing consumption behaviors towards a growing number of citizens and communities that embrace sustainable lifestyles and engage in the green transition process.
The intended shifts to change are leveraged throughout 4 interlinked priority areas of work/pillars: (1) decarbonization and climate resilience (2) circular economy (3) depollution and (4) nature and biodiversity. Interventions to be financed by Sweden will support pillars: Decarbonization and climate resilience and Depollution.
Under the Decarbonization and Climate Resilience Pillar, the Green Transition Portfolio contribution would consist of implementing interconnected interventions focused on: a) understanding and enabling policy and regulatory work to advance the energy poverty challenge, b) advancing energy efficiency retrofits and renewable energy investments, c) accelerating e-mobility, and, d) minimising the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) impact.
Under the Depollution Pillar, the Green Transition Portfolio contribution would consist of implementing interconnected interventions focused on the following distinct intervention areas: a) enhancing legal frameworks and building capacities to improve the management of hazardous waste and chemicals, especially Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs), b) supporting remediation of contaminated industrial sites and building for effective environmental management,) engaging academic institutions in research to inform policy design and implement innovative remediation techniques, and) promoting green chemistry in key industries through stakeholder engagement, environmental audits, and financial support mechanisms) strengthening environmental rule of law in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is anticipated that a first change shift, in terms of fulfilling portfolio outcome level targets, will take place by year 2029. Sweden's support will initially cover a three year period, while a continuation of activities will be decided in 2027 based on lessons learned from first phase.

The Green Transition Portfolio is designed as a systemic transformation response, focusing on three key shifts: institutional governance - from fragmented to outcome-driven governance; economic transformation from linear to circular economies; and social engagement - from passive to engaged citizens and markets.
Based on the results achieved under the pillars and following an intensive involvement of stakeholders, annual report for 2025 summarized progress per each shift:
- Institutional governance - progress is modest and uneven due to weak institutional capacities, slow legal processes, lack of evidence-based decision making and structured monitoring, as well as fragmentation of responsibilities across all pillars;
- Economic transformation this is strongest shift across the portfolio due to the fact that the industry is more ready for transition than institutions, showing demand for audits, ESCO models and CE practices, growing private-sector interest driven by EU standards, CBAM pressures and cost efficiency.
- Social engagement - This shift shows the weakest overall progress resulting from no meaningful societal engagement in energy transition and environment protection and with only early community-level signals (farmer networks, waste container systems) in depollution and circular economy.
From 1 January to 31 December 2025 key portfolio results contributing to the above changes are:
Pillar 1 Decarbonisation and Climate Resilience:
EU-aligned energy poverty framework in BiH has been advanced through research tools, gender-responsive assessment, partnerships, stakeholder engagement (including ministries responsible for social protection, energy, and statistics) and capacity building for inclusive policies. Energy efficency (EE) and Renewable Energy Sources (RES) investments have progressed through the support to 23 underdeveloped municipalities, green financing, Energy Service companies (ESCO) market development, and gender-responsive monitoring of social impacts. The Green Finance Scheme, implemented in cooperation with Union Banka, remained operational and continued mobilizing private sector investments into green transition measures. E-mobility activities advanced policy, financing and infrastructure planning, regulatory alignment with EU standards, stakeholder coordination, including the Chamber of Commerce of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Association for E-Mobility. Carbon Border adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) readiness has been improved through institutional coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations of Bosnia and Herzegovina (MOFTER), chambers of commerce, electricity utilities, and international partners development of a national CBAM handbook, Monitoring, reporting and Verification (MRV) capacity building, emissions reporting support, and private sector preparedness in BiH. Country wide Hydromet network assessment was completed with 63 hydromet stations procured.
Pillar 2 Depollution:
Interventions strengthened hazardous waste and chemicals management through legal support, institutional cooperation, EU alignment, technical assessments and capacity building on waste control and trafficking. Contaminated site management was improved through pilot site assessments, remediation planning, hotspot mapping, and coordination under Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions. Two pilot sites Sarajevo International Airport and the Sheep Dip site in Sokolac/Drakseni were validated for further decontamination interventions. The remediation and recultivation plan for the contaminated acid tar pits site in Modria was completed during 2025. Green chemistry and circular economy were promoted in Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) through training design, stakeholder outreach, and a technical support programme. Environmental rule of law was strengthened through judicial training MoUs, seminars on environmental crime, student fieldwork, and preparation of case law analysis in BiH. The main actors targeted through the actions are Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations of Bosnia and Herzegovina (MOFTER) for the preparation of the Rulebook on professional training for persons handling ozone-depleting substances, Brko District for drafting the Waste Management Law, the Federal Ministry of Environment and Tourism for the preparation of the five-year Federal Waste Management Plan, Ministries of Health of RBIH and Republika srpsaka, Chamber of Commerce of Republika Srpska and the Chamber of Economy of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina regarding application of Green Chemistry, judicial and prosecutorial training centres of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska for long-term cooperation in the environmental law training programmes
Pillar 3 - Biodiversity and Nature:
Management plans for nine protected areas were finalized, six of which have been adopted. Restoration plan for the Protected Habitat Tiina has been completed targeting 196 ha of wetland for restoration in 2026. Biodiversity expenditure reviews, which create a base for Biodiversity Finance Plans, were completed.
Pillar 4 Circular Economy:
Preparatory work was undertaken to establish the Circular Economy Academy, including development of its conceptual framework. Revision of the Circular Economy Roadmap, and development of its Action Plan was initiated. Activities focused on SME acceleration were implemented jointly with the Depollution Pillar. Under this pollar, UNDP continued to support the development of four sectoral strategies in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in close cooperation with the Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry and the Chamber of Commerce of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The supported sectors include construction materials, metal and electrical industry, wood processing, and mining and mineral raw materials.
During year 2025, the Portfolio established its governance and operational foundations through the creation of a Steering Board, co-chaired by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations (MoFTER) and the UN Resident Coordinator, while UNDP, UNEP, UNODC and UN Women formalized their collaboration through UN-to-UN agreements. Advisory Committees were formed to strengthen the cross-sector dialogue. An onboarding session introduced portfolio management approaches and Microsoft Loop as a coordination and learning platform. An inception workshop gathered over 50 representatives from government, private sector, academia and civil society, complemented by bilateral consultations advancing alignment on e-mobility, energy poverty, CBAM readiness, environmental justice, green chemistry and circular economy.
Cross-cutting work included validation of the Monitoring evaluation and learning (MEL) framework, development of gender and communications strategies, and continued resource mobilization, with additional funding secured for several pillars.
A dedicated Gender Action Plan (GAP) was developed and embedded within the overall portfolio governance structure, results framework, monitoring mechanisms, and implementation modalities. The GAP ensures that Bosnia and Herzegovinas green transition advances as an inclusive and gender-responsive just transition and focuses on three interconnected dimensions: (i) strengthening gender-responsive policies and legislation; (ii) increasing womens participation in decision-making and governance processes; and (iii) expanding womens access to green jobs, finance, entrepreneurship opportunities, and emerging green value chains.
Going forward, the Portfolio will continue strengthening partnerships with UN Women, institutions, academia, civil society, and private sector actors to further mainstream gender equality and ensure that the green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina delivers equitable social, economic, and environmental benefits for all. Initial implementation in 2025 demonstrated encouraging progress across all four pillars of the portfolio.
At the portfolio level, implementation of the Gender Action Plan has already contributed to establishing foundational mechanisms for gender-responsive green transition governance. Coordination structures, including the Steering Committee, Advisory Group, and Gender and Climate Coalition, have become operational and currently engage more than 60 institutions and stakeholders. Early results also indicate growing momentum in womens participation, institutional awareness, and the development of pipelines for women-led green entrepreneurship.
